notes:
Overview: TideHaven is a payments-first ecommerce platform with an internal CX stack. Evaluating Redwood for automating agent workflows + reliable tool-calling to internal ticketing and payments APIs.

Primary asks:
- Tool-calling: create/update tickets in internal TicketAPI, initiate refunds via PaymentsAPI, escalate L2 with PagerDuty trigger. Need idempotent calls and clear success/failure semantics.
- Agent assist + summarization: live agent snippets, end-of-call summary + suggested next actions (refund, escalate, resolve). Must produce short (1-3 sentence) summaries for agent handoff.
- Reliability under spikes: Black Friday-style load: expected peak bursts ~10x normal for 6-12h; want graceful degradation (queueing, async webhook fallback) not errors.
- Latency/throughput targets: p95 < 200ms for generation step in agent UI; support 120 QPS at peak for tool-calling orchestration; concurrency target ~300 active agent sessions.
- Model preferences: prefer smaller quantized LLMs for tool-calls and summarization to save cost but want ability to route to higher-quality model for flagged escalations. Interested in model pinning + automatic fallback.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, keys in KMS/HSM, audit logs retained 5 years, EU data residency for EU customers, SOC2 attestation required.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (Jordan Park) — high level fit, demo requested.
- 2026-02-02: Technical discovery with SE (Maya) — reviewed TicketAPI spec, PaymentsAPI, auth flow. Noted idempotency gaps on PaymentsAPI.
- 2026-02-11: Fireflies recording ff_20260211_7a3b2c — key quote from Head of CX: "We cannot have refunds failing silently; idempotency and clear retry logic are non-negotiable."
- 2026-02-22: Internal security questionnaire sent; asked for SOC2 + sample audit logging format.
- 2026-03-01: Demo of dedicated routing and canary tool-calls — ops liked fallback webhooks.
- 2026-03-09: Architecture call — agreed on POC scope, received Drive docs for POC plan and security FAQ.

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 1: Sandbox onboarding, SSO test, import TicketAPI swagger, basic create/update ticket flows.
- Week 2: Implement Refund flow as tool-call with idempotency token + reconciliation job. Run synthetic spike test (10x).
- Success criteria: <1% failed tool-calls under 10x load with clear retry paths; accurate summaries (>=85% agent-verified); audit log entries for every tool-call.

Integration notes / red flags:
- PaymentsAPI currently returns non-deterministic error codes; need pre-POC dev task to normalize (Jira: INTEG-215).
- EU legal requires data residency confirmation before we send real customer data; initial POC can use synthetic/eu-anonymized dataset.
- Agent UI currently expects sync success; plan to implement optimistic UI + eventual reconciliation for refunds to preserve UX during spikes.

Quotes / customer voice:
- "If we can automate the 60% of refunds that are transactional without manual review, ops cost drops significantly." — Head of CX
- "We need clear rollback semantics for refund tool-calls. No double refunds." — Payments Lead

- Legal to confirm data residency path for EU unit, attach SOC2 docs to Drive (Jordan/Luis).

Internal action items:

Status summary: Qualified enterprise account, moving to POC during March; main risks are Payments API normalization and EU residency confirmation. High chance to convert if POC validates reliability under spikes and tool-calling safety mechanics.
